<atm-task id="CI-1844-lint" phase="ci-fix" mode="fix">
  <description>PR #1844 (fix/rustls-0.23.46) fails CI: 'Just lint (ubuntu-latest)' is the only failing check. Root-cause the lint failure and fix it on this branch. Run the failing job log first: https://github.com/randlee/atm-core/actions/runs/38670420214/job/116212002884. If the cause is Windows-specific, xwin is available for cross-checking.</description>

  <branch>fix/rustls-0.23.46</branch>
  <worktree>../atm-core-worktrees/fix-rustls-0.23.46</worktree>
  <pr-target>develop</pr-target>
  <stack-discipline>`fix/rustls-0.23.46` is a layer cut from the current top of the phase stack; `develop` is the layer directly below it. Work only on this layer. Never edit, push to, rebase, or open a PR against any layer below, and never wait for a lower layer's QA or CI. If `develop` gains commits while you work, run `git fetch origin && git merge origin/develop` once at task start and once before the final push; the parent wins where copies differ. Once this task closes the layer is frozen: every later finding against it is fixed on a new layer cut from the top of the stack, never here.</stack-discipline>
  <authoritative-sprint-doc>docs/team-protocol.md</authoritative-sprint-doc>

  <dependency-relations>
- See authoritative sprint doc.
  </dependency-relations>

  <finding-ids>
CI-1844-lint
  </finding-ids>

  <triage-records>

  </triage-records>

  <required-fixes>
Root-cause the 'Just lint' failure (read the job log: gh run view --log-failed, one call) and fix the cause, not the gate. No gate weakening, no suppression.
  </required-fixes>

  <acceptance-criteria>
`just lint` passes locally on the pushed head; the fix is the minimal root-cause change; report cause in the close.
  </acceptance-criteria>

  <validation-requirements>
just lint (and just test if code changed)
  </validation-requirements>

  <references>
https://github.com/randlee/atm-core/actions/runs/38670420214/job/116212002884
  </references>

  <workflow>
    <step id="a">Start the task immediately with `atm task start CI-1844-lint "<one line: what you will do first>"`, then begin executing it in the same work session unless blocked.</step>
    <step id="b">Read `docs/team-protocol.md` before editing. Treat it as the authoritative source for sprint scope, retained requirements, deletion targets, validation, and acceptance criteria. If this assignment summary and the sprint doc differ, the sprint doc wins and the mismatch must be reported.</step>
    <step id="c">Update the assigned worktree from the target branch before editing. Include all earlier-sprint fixes already merged forward to that branch.</step>
    <step id="c1">Honor the `<dependency-relations>` block above: must-follow merge-forward trigger is parent dev push, not QA; merge parent → child before every round. PR-completion trigger is parent PR merge first. Stop if a parallel-safe relation intersects.</step>
    <step id="d">Read the referenced triage records first. Treat the listed occurrences as the minimum required scope on this branch.</step>
    <step id="d2">Before fixing each finding, verify the defect it describes is still actually present at the cited file:line in this worktree's current state. If a finding does not reproduce — already fixed, superseded by other work, or the described code path no longer exists — refuse to perform speculative or invented work to "address" it. Do not edit unrelated code in its name. Note it in your push/validation report as `not-reproducible` with the file:line you checked instead, and skip it. This applies per-finding, not to the whole task — fix every finding that does reproduce as normal.</step>
    <step id="e">Fix every promoted-branch occurrence in scope. Do not stop at the first location when the triage record marks the finding as repeatable.</step>
    <step id="f">As soon as the branch is pushable, commit and push immediately. Send branch name and commit hash right away to the assigner (the sender of this message) with a plain `atm send team-lead --stdin` — a progress report, not a close; never close the task on a push. This lets follow-up QA start in parallel. </step>
    <step id="g">Run the required validation after the push report. While it is FAIL, keep fixing and report progress with plain `atm send`. When it is PASS, push, and close the task with the validation report rendered from the fix-complete template: `atm task close CI-1844-lint completed --template .claude/skills/codex-orchestration/fix-complete.md.j2 --vars <scratch>/fix-complete-CI-1844-lint-vars.json`. Build the vars from that template's `required_variables`: `task_id` and `phase` unchanged from this assignment, `commit` the final pushed head, the gate output lines, and per finding fixed or `not-reproducible` with the file:line checked. Write the vars file outside the repository and never commit it. Only this close frees your queue: the next assignment stays queued and never starts until `CI-1844-lint` is closed, and a plain `atm send` report does not close it. Use `atm task close CI-1844-lint refused "<reason>"` only when the whole assignment cannot be done. </step>
    <step id="h">After the close, read ATM again: the next queued task starts only now.</step>
  </workflow>
</atm-task>

<atm-task id="atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix" sprint="bh-3" mode="fix">
  <description><![CDATA[Fix `atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix` (found in sprint bh-3). `bd show atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix` is the assignment: a poured fix bead carries the finding in its description and `metadata.remedy`; a finding bead has the finding and evidence in its description, the remedy in its design, and when it is fixed in its acceptance criteria.]]></description>

  <worktree><![CDATA[/Users/randlee/github/atm-bd-orchestration-worktrees/fix/bh-3-qa-r2]]></worktree>
  <branch><![CDATA[fix/bh-3-qa-r2]]></branch>
  <stack><![CDATA[phase-bh]]></stack>
  <pr-target><![CDATA[fix/bh-3-qa-r1]]></pr-target>
  <stack-discipline><![CDATA[The finding is on a frozen layer. `fix/bh-3-qa-r2` is a new layer cut from `origin/fix/bh-3-qa-r1`, the top of stack `phase-bh` at dispatch; its PR lands on the stack's current top. Work only on this branch. The task assigner is the stack writer: never run `gh stack link`, `sync`, `rebase` or `merge`.]]></stack-discipline>

  <workflow>
    <step id="a"><![CDATA[Before claiming, in the worktree run `git fetch origin` (no rebase: the branch was cut from the stack top, and check (5), `--is-ancestor`, proves it holds `origin/fix/bh-3-qa-r1`), then `/Users/randlee/github/atm-core/.claude/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/assignment-gates.py dev --root atm-phase-bh --bead atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --pr-target fix/bh-3-qa-r1 --worktree /Users/randlee/github/atm-bd-orchestration-worktrees/fix/bh-3-qa-r2` (scripts come from the primary checkout, never the branch). Checks, commands and refusal codes: (1) plan valid: `/Users/randlee/github/atm-core/.claude/skills/atm-beads/scripts/validate-plan --root atm-phase-bh` exits 0, else `PLAN_INVALID`; (2) ready: `bd ready -n 0 --json` lists the bead, else `NOT_READY`; (3) claimable without `--force`: `bd show atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --json` shows status `open` and assignee empty or `$ATM_IDENTITY`, else `UNCLAIMABLE`; (4) target: `metadata.pr_target` is `fix/bh-3-qa-r1` or `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<metadata.pr_target> origin/fix/bh-3-qa-r1` exits 0 (`pr_target` is a lower bound), else `PR_TARGET_MISMATCH`; (5) base: `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/fix/bh-3-qa-r1 HEAD` exits 0, else `WRONG_BASE`; any command failing: `GATE_CANNOT_RUN`. On refusal, reuse an existing workflow class bead with the same failure signature: append the task id, head, command and failure evidence, and cite its id in the refusal; if none matches, report the signature to the task assigner for classification and cite that message instead; never create a per-task shadow or delay the refusal. On pass, claim with `bd update atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --claim --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"`, then start `atm task start atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix "<one line: what you will do first>"`.]]></step>
    <step id="a1"><![CDATA[When it prints `NOT_READY` the bead is not ready: do not claim it or start the task. Find the root cause: `bd show atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix` (status, assignee), `bd blocked --json | jq --arg b atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix '.[] | select(.id == $b)'` (open blockers: another fix that must land first), and `bd show <blocker>` for each. Then refuse; never wait: close the task with `atm task close atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix refused --template .claude/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/templates/task-refused.md.j2 --vars <scratch>/refused-atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix-vars.json`, `bead_state` `open`, `reason_md` giving the bead, why it is not ready, which bead or agent must move, and, for a blocker not yet its dependency, the edge to add, `bd dep add atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --blocked-by <blocker>`, so `bd ready` lists the bead only once the blocker closes. The task assigner then re-assigns it.]]></step>
    <step id="b"><![CDATA[Read `bd show atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix`, then its `metadata.sprint_bead`, the sprint whose contract its requirements and ADRs come from, for the scope it belongs to. Read every id in the bead's own `metadata.requirements` and `metadata.adrs` (requirements: /Users/randlee/github/atm-core/docs/plans/phase-bh/anchors.json; ADRs: NONE); the fix must keep satisfying them. Before editing, read the repository QA policy `.claude/project/quality-policy.md` and every guideline it names for the languages this fix touches.]]></step>
    <step id="c"><![CDATA[Before fixing, verify the defect still exists at the cited file:line in this worktree. If it does not reproduce (already fixed, superseded, or code path gone), do no speculative or invented work for it: close it as not reproducible (step f), citing the file:line you checked.]]></step>
    <step id="d"><![CDATA[Read the complete finding and remedy and list every required task; create an itemized private checklist outside the tracked tree with every task identified, and work through the checklist one item at a time. Fix every occurrence in scope, not just the first: for a repeatable pattern, search the worktree for it and fix each one. Touch only the files the remedy needs. Then go through the checklist again one item at a time, confirming each is done. Run `cd apps/atm-bd-console && uv run pytest -q` and `cd apps/atm-bd-console && uv run ruff check src tests` until they pass with zero failures; a lint failure inherited from a lower layer is yours to fix on this layer.]]></step>
    <step id="d1"><![CDATA[If the work needs a change other live branches need at the same time (a shared type or trait signature, or a critical bug every branch carries), stop that edit, tell the task assigner the exact change and the branches it breaks, follow the assigner's base (`.claude/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/SKILL.md`, Parallel Quick Fix), and report a quick-fix PR you open by plain `atm send`.]]></step>
    <step id="e"><![CDATA[Rebase onto the stack's current top (it may have moved since dispatch): `git fetch origin`; the top is what `/Users/randlee/github/atm-core/.claude/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/scripts/assignment-gates.py stack-top --pr-target fix/bh-3-qa-r1` prints on exit 0 (from GitHub's stacks); any other exit prints a code (`STACK_AMBIGUOUS`, `GATE_CANNOT_RUN`): never guess, refuse with it by step f1. Then `git rebase origin/<top>`, re-run `cd apps/atm-bd-console && uv run pytest -q` and `cd apps/atm-bd-console && uv run ruff check src tests`, and `git push --force-with-lease origin fix/bh-3-qa-r2`. Unless this quick-fix branch already has its open PR, open it against that top: `gh pr create --base <top> --head fix/bh-3-qa-r2 --fill` (never `--draft`); run `/sc-gh-stack-view` (read-only) and keep its output verbatim. Record the full head SHA, the top as `rebased_onto`, and the PR number and url.]]></step>
    <step id="f"><![CDATA[Close the bead and task together, `bd close` first; close the task only if `bd close` succeeded: `bd close atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --reason "fixed at <short sha>" --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"` (or `--reason "not reproducible: <file:line checked>"`), then `atm task close atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix completed --template .claude/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/templates/fix-complete.md.j2 --vars <scratch>/fix-complete-atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix-vars.json`. Build the vars from that template's `required_variables`: `task_id` and `sprint` unchanged, `commit` the pushed head, `rebased_onto` the top, `pr_number` and `pr_url` from step e, `stack_view` the verbatim `/sc-gh-stack-view` output (omit these five for `not_reproducible`), the outcome, and the gate output lines; write the vars file outside the repository. The fix then gets its own sanity check and QA (the group's sanity and qa beads, which the lead created with this assignment for an important or minor finding; a quick-fix finding has no sanity check, only the quick fix's next QA bead). Only this close frees your queue.]]></step>
    <step id="f1"><![CDATA[If the fix cannot be done at all, reuse an existing workflow class bead for the same failure signature: append the task id, head, command and failure evidence, and cite the class id in the refusal. If no class matches, report the signature to the task assigner for classification and cite that message instead; never create a per-task shadow or delay the refusal. Also announce a serious infrastructure failure once per cause to the oversight recipients (`.claude/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/SKILL.md` Lead Role). Leave the bead open with `bd update atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --status open --assignee "" --append-notes "FIX_CANNOT_COMPLETE; workflow class or escalation <reference>: <reason>" --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"` and close the task with `atm task close atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix refused --template .claude/skills/atm-bd-orchestration/templates/task-refused.md.j2 --vars <scratch>/refused-atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix-vars.json`. The fixer never closes a fix or finding bead unfixed; only quality-mgr (ceremony) or the task assigner does. A blocker is not a failure: if the task needs unfinished work another bead or agent owns (a prerequisite open or reopened, another agent's fix not landed), stop, return the bead with `bd update atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --status open --assignee "" --append-notes "BLOCKED: <blocker>: <why>" --actor "$ATM_IDENTITY"` and close the task `refused` as above (`bead_state` `open`), its `reason_md` naming the blocker and the edge `bd dep add atm-bh-3.f4-r2-fix --blocked-by <blocker>`; never stay active waiting. A shared change you can make yourself is not a blocker: it is a Parallel Quick Fix (step d1) and the task continues.]]></step>
    <step id="g"><![CDATA[After the close, read ATM again: the next queued task starts only now.]]></step>
  </workflow>
</atm-task>
